description:
Worktree identity is stored in the data root, so checkouts sharing an out-of-repo store overwrite one another's identity on every command and report a false relocation.

## Background

The identity file is `<data root>/worktree.json`, read and rewritten by `crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_identity.rs`. A data root inside a checkout has one owner, so one file is enough. A store outside the checkout can serve many checkouts.

Observed with jit 1.0.0 and one external data root used from a primary checkout and a linked worktree:

- The file holds whichever checkout wrote last. It held the linked worktree's id, branch and root after commands had run from both checkouts.
- A command run after switching checkout warned `Worktree relocated: <one checkout> -> <the other>`, although neither checkout moved.

The relocation warning therefore loses its meaning, and a checkout's identity depends on which checkout ran last.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each checkout using a shared external data root has one stable worktree id, unchanged by commands run from other checkouts.
- [hard] REQ-02: Alternating commands between two checkouts on one external data root emit no relocation warning.
- [hard] REQ-03: Moving a checkout with `git worktree move` still reports one relocation and keeps its id.
- [hard] REQ-04: A data root inside a checkout keeps its current identity behaviour, including new identity for a copied worktree.
- [hard] REQ-05: Concurrent commands from two checkouts leave each identity intact.
- [hard] REQ-06: The storage-format reference states where identity lives for each layout.

## Notes

- The identity location for an external data root is an implementation choice. The checkout's own git directory is the likely home.
- @/issue/1b7f58ae changes how the identity file is published, so the two changes touch the same code.
title: Checkouts sharing an external data root keep separate worktree identities
